record.original_question: Is every cubic, 3-connected, bipartite planar graph Hamiltonian?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.7 Every cubic 3-connected bipartite planar graph is Hamiltonian.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph that is simultaneously:
(i) cubic, i.e. every vertex has degree exactly $3$;
(ii) $3$-connected, i.e. $G$ has at least $4$ vertices and removing any $2$ vertices leaves a connected graph;
(iii) bipartite, i.e. its vertex set can be partitioned into two independent sets; and
(iv) planar, i.e. $G$ admits an embedding in the plane without edge crossings.

A Hamiltonian cycle of $G$ is a cycle that visits every vertex of $G$ exactly once.

Prove or disprove: every graph $G$ satisfying (i)–(iv) admits a Hamiltonian cycle.
artifact.status_search_result: Barnette's conjecture remains open as of 2025. Recent partial progress includes verification that no counterexample exists with fewer than 86 vertices, and a 2025 result establishing Hamiltonicity for cubic 3-connected bipartite planar graphs whose faces all have size at most 8. No proof or counterexample of the full conjecture is known.

status_evidence.title: Barnette's conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Barnette's conjecture is an unsolved problem in graph theory... stating that every bipartite polyhedral graph with three edges per vertex has a Hamiltonian cycle.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is currently listed as an unsolved problem.

status_evidence.title: Barnette Graphs with Faces up to Size 8 are Hamiltonian
status_evidence.snippet: Hamiltonicity for cubic, bipartite, planar and 2-connected graphs with faces of size up to 8.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress in 2025 addresses only graphs with bounded face size, leaving the general conjecture open.
